description:
On fz-i89 6ed56d515 (includes fz-28p), debug build, fz2 interp:
- 2,000 bindings a_i = x + i followed by a1 + a2 + ... + a2000 (scratchpad/s75e/varsum2000.fz): 'fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting' in the compiler's main thread. With ulimit -s 65520 it compiles and prints 2001000.
- 2,000 sequential calls whose results are summed (seqsum2000.fz): same overflow; with the larger stack it prints 2003000.
- Controls that pass at 2,000: the same bindings returning only a2000 (varlast2000.fz); a sum of 2,000 constants (addonly2000.fz); x + x + ... 2,000 times (xsum2000.fz); 2,000 calls returning only the last (seqnosum2000.fz).
So the trigger is many distinct values live at once across a long chain, and the depth is the compiler's recursion, not generated code. At 1,000 it passes.
Not investigated: which compiler function recurses per live value or per step (profile with the stack limit lowered, or run under lldb and read the repeating frame).
Fails before, passes after: varsum2000 and seqsum2000 compile and print on interp with the default stack; a telemetry or stack-depth test pins that the recursion does not grow with the number of live values.
Acceptance: full gate green; no pin rises unexplained.
title: The compiler does not overflow its own stack on a body of 2,000 live values
